features.gap: Only create/drop/drop_and_create derived from the model's own columns (not a free-form table definition). No `if_not_exists`, `force: :cascade`, `temporary`, `comment`, `id: :uuid/false`, composite PK options, or `drop_table if_exists/cascade` options. No indexes, FKs, or check constraints at create time. Spec asserts exact SQL only for the active adapter.

features.feature: Micrate integration — versioned SQL migration files (Up/Down)
features.gap: No Micrate reference in src/ or spec/; only docs. Versioned files, up/down, and the tracking table are wholly external. Grant offers no way to run a Crystal migration class or to call Micrate from a Grant API.
Hand-written SQL Up/Down only. No `change` with automatic inverse, no `reversible`/`revert`/`up_only`, and no IrreversibleMigration error.
CLI lives in Amber/Micrate outside this repo. Grant provides no task API (create/drop database, migrate, rollback, status, seed) that a CLI can call, and no spec exists.

Maps only Bool, Float32/64, Int32/64, String, Time, UUID, created_at/updated_at (+ PG arrays). No mapping for Int8/Int16, Decimal/BigDecimal with precision/scale, Bytes, JSON::Any/jsonb, Date, Enum, Time precision, or text vs string with limit. These raise at migrate time. Spec asserts the SQL only for the current adapter.
No dump, no load, no schema file format, and no introspection layer to build one from.

No index DSL. The model-based Migrator emits no indexes or unique constraints, even for `unique` columns. Missing options: unique, name, where (partial), using, order, opclass, include, expression indexes, algorithm concurrently, if_not_exists, length. No index introspection.
No FK DDL from Grant, no `references`/`foreign_key: true` in table definitions, no on_delete/on_update/deferrable/validate options, no introspection. Model `belongs_to` does not emit an FK.
No DSL, no introspection, no `validate:` option, no `t.check_constraint`.

Only Crystal literal defaults (String, Number, Bool, nil) become SQL DEFAULT. No SQL-expression defaults (`default: -> { "now()" }`, `gen_random_uuid()`), no `change_column_default`, and non-literal Crystal defaults silently produce no DDL default.
Only a convention (a Crystal script); no `Grant::Seed` runner, no `db/seeds.cr` lookup, no idempotent-seed helper, and no spec.
No Grant code reads or writes schema_migrations or ar_internal_metadata (environment protection). No current_version, status, pending check, or per-database migration paths.

features.feature: Encryption migration helpers (data migration for encrypted columns)
features.gap: rotate_encryption is exercised on SQLite (8 examples pass). encrypt_column, decrypt_column and generate_migration have no spec. The helpers loop with `limit/offset` and `save!` per row (offset paging skips rows if the predicate changes), and no PG/MySQL run.
Scaffolding lives in the separate Amber CLI project; nothing in Grant's src/ or specs. No name-parsing (AddXToY -> add_column) inside Grant.

features.feature: alter_table / change_column / add_column at runtime via Grant DSL
features.gap: No ALTER TABLE DSL of any kind (add/remove/change column, null, default, change_table bulk). SQLite needs a table rebuild for change_column.
No rename_table DSL (which in AR also renames the pk sequence and indexes).
No rename_column/rename_index; AR also renames default-named indexes on column rename.
No join-table DDL helper (name derivation from two tables, FK columns, optional index).

features.feature: references / belongs_to columns in migrations (add_reference, remove_reference, polymorphic)
features.gap: No reference helper; polymorphic `_type`/`_id` pair, index, and FK creation must be hand-written.
Model `timestamps` yields created_at/updated_at in create_sql (VARCHAR on SQLite), but there is no add_timestamps/remove_timestamps or `precision:` option, and no NOT NULL on the timestamp columns.

features.feature: Column options: null, limit, precision, scale, comment, collation, array
features.gap: Nullability is derived from Crystal nilability, and `column_type:` allows a verbatim SQL type. There are no `limit`, `precision`, `scale`, `comment`, or `collation` options. Arrays are PG-only via type table.
No comment DDL (PG COMMENT ON, MySQL COMMENT clause; SQLite unsupported).

features.feature: Introspection: table_exists?, column_exists?, columns, tables, primary_key, indexes, foreign_keys

features.gap: Grant's columns are declared at compile time in the model, so there is no runtime column cache to reset or dump. A drift check between model and DB would need introspection (see introspection row).
features.not_applicable_reason: Ruby lazily reads columns from the DB and caches them; Grant declares columns at compile time, so a runtime column cache does not exist. The compile-time schema is the source of truth.

features.feature: Migration class: up/down/change with versioned class ([8.0] compat)
features.gap: No Migration base class or per-version compatibility layer; migrations are SQL files for external Micrate. Compat layers (ActiveRecord::Migration::Compatibility) are Rails-history specific.

features.feature: MigrationContext operations: migrate to version, rollback(step), redo, up/down(version), forward, status
features.gap: None present in Grant; must go through Micrate CLI.
No migration runner, so no per-migration transaction wrapping and no opt-out (needed for CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY on PG). MySQL does not support transactional DDL.

features.feature: Migration output and helpers: say, say_with_time, announce, suppress_messages
features.gap: No migration runner output layer; could reuse Grant::Log.
No detection of pending migrations at boot/in specs and no auto load of the test schema.
No metadata table storing environment, so destructive tasks (drop/reset) in production are not blocked. `Migrator#drop_and_create` is unguarded.
No DDL. Migrator never emits UNIQUE, even for validates_uniqueness_of fields.

features.feature: Composite primary keys and primary key options in table creation
features.gap: Migrator handles a single `primary: true` column (Int auto or UUID/String) and raises without one. Composite PK models exist (src/grant/composite_primary_key.cr) but the Migrator emits a single-column PK only; `id: false` tables (join tables) unsupported.

No view DDL or view-backed model helpers; `view_exists?`/`views` introspection absent. Deferred: Low value, and needs PG-specific refresh semantics. Raw execute covers it until the DDL DSL (M02b) is stable.

features.feature: PostgreSQL enum types, extensions, and custom column types (create_enum, enable_extension, hstore, citext, jsonb, inet, ltree, money)
features.gap: No DDL for enums or extensions; type table lacks these types. `column_type:` verbatim works as a workaround.

No DDL for generated columns; must use verbatim `column_type:`. Deferred: Low value and overlaps the Infrastructure virtual-column row. Verbatim column_type: works as a workaround. Do both together later.

features.feature: execute (raw DDL inside a migration) and schema-qualified table names
features.gap: Model.exec works for raw SQL (out of scope). Missing: a migration-scoped `execute` that respects the runner's connection and dry run, plus schema-qualified DDL names across all DSL calls (quote handles dotted names).

features.feature: Multi-database migrations (per-connection migrations_paths, db:migrate:primary, connection-specific tasks)
features.gap: Grant has named connections and sharding, but no migration runner targets one by name, and there is no per-connection schema_migrations. Schema-tenant (PG search_path) migrations across tenants are also absent.

features.feature: Database tasks: create/drop database, purge, structure dump (structure.sql), setup/reset/prepare, truncate_all
features.gap: No Grant API; Micrate/Amber CLI does create/drop only. No structure dump/load, purge, `db:prepare`, `db:reset`, or `truncate_all`.

features.feature: Schema format configuration (:ruby vs :sql) and db:schema:load for fresh environments
features.gap: Depends on the schema dump row; nothing to select or load.
No migration runner and no advisory-lock helper in Grant, so two deploy nodes can run the same DDL concurrently.

features.feature: Migration file generator naming conventions (AddXToY, CreateXs parse, timestamped versions)
features.gap: Covered only inside the external Amber CLI row; no attribute parsing DSL in Grant.

features.feature: Metaprogrammed migration lookup: Migration.method_missing forwarding to connection, and ActiveRecord::Migration.[] compatibility shims
features.not_applicable_reason: Rails forwards unknown migration methods to the connection through method_missing, and keeps version shims for Ruby-era default changes. Grant has no legacy versions to shim and would define typed methods.

features.gap: Core encrypt/decrypt, deterministic lookup, nil handling and rotation work. Cipher is AES-256-CBC+HMAC, not AES-GCM. Storage uses a separate <attr>_encrypted column instead of transparent same-name column. Only String attributes. Missing options: previous:, ignore_case:, downcase:, compress:, key_provider:, encryptor:, message_serializer:, per-attribute support_unencrypted_data:. Rotation specs are SQLite-only.

DSL, detection, key tuple helpers and find/exists? signatures exist (12 passing SQLite examples, config only). Persistence is unimplemented: composite_primary_key/transactions.cr is an empty TODO module, so create/update/destroy/reload rely on the single-key path. No spec inserts and reads back a composite-key row. Missing AR parts: find with array of tuples, where(id: [[a,b],...]), to_param/id as Array, associations with composite foreign keys, primary_key: [..] on belongs_to/has_many.

pg.cr maps Array(String/Int/Float/Bool) to TEXT[]/INT[]/etc. and type.cr has from_rs for arrays. No spec covers array round-trip, and the cited specs are JSON and numeric converters, not arrays. Query operators (ANY, @>, &&, array_length), array_append/remove helpers and UUID/Time arrays are absent.

Grant::Serializers::JSONB class exists but stores plain JSON text; specs are converter unit specs only, no DB round-trip or PG jsonb column. Missing: native jsonb column type in migrations, operators (->, ->>, @>, ?, #>), where(data: {a: 1}) containment, store_accessor, in-place mutation dirty tracking.

Only auto-generation of a v4 UUID on save is specced. Not proven: reload/round-trip through the DB, find/find_by by UUID string or UUID, UUID primary key, invalid-string casting, PG native uuid column vs CHAR(36) on MySQL/SQLite, gen_random_uuid() DB default.
No YAML fixture loader, no label-to-id hashing, no fixture accessors, no transactional-test wrapper.
No adapter API for advisory locks. Rationale for n.a. (not core) is not a Ruby-metaprogramming reason; AR ships these as adapter methods used by the migrator.

features.feature: QueryLogs with context tags (SQL comment injection)
features.gap: annotate exists per query, but no global tag config, no fiber-local context, no automatic prepend of model/controller/action/job tags.

Column name lock_version is hard-coded in src/grant/locking/optimistic.cr (declares column and builds the WHERE). No locking_column override, no automatic activation when a lock_version column exists, no lock_optimistically toggle.
No API to scope find/update/destroy/reload by multiple columns while keeping a single-column primary key (for example a sharded or tenant-partitioned key).

features.feature: Encryption: previous: schemes for key/scheme migration
features.gap: Only one active key; rotation is a batch re-encrypt helper (MigrationHelpers.rotate_encryption), not read-with-old, write-with-new. No multiple primary keys and no per-attribute previous schemes, so a rotation requires a maintenance window.
Not supported by the encrypts macro; case-insensitive deterministic lookup requires the caller to downcase manually.
No compression before encrypting; large text columns are stored uncompressed.

features.feature: Encryption: support_unencrypted_data and per-attribute plaintext fallback
features.gap: Config.support_unencrypted_data exists and EncryptedAttribute#decrypt honors it, but the macro-generated getter calls Grant::Encryption.decrypt, which does not; no spec exercises the flag. Also no per-attribute override and no way to query plaintext + ciphertext together during migration.

features.feature: Encryption: transparent same-name column and non-String attribute types
features.gap: encrypts creates a virtual String accessor over a <attr>_encrypted column; the original column name is not usable, where(email: ...) is not rewritten, and Int/Time/JSON values cannot be encrypted.

features.feature: Encryption context and record helpers (encrypted_attribute?, ciphertext_for, encrypt, decrypt, without_encryption, protecting_encrypted_data)
features.gap: encrypted_attributes registry exists but there is no instance ciphertext_for/encrypted_attribute?/encrypt/decrypt, and no scoped blocks to disable or pin encryption (keys, encryptor) per fiber.

features.feature: Encryption: pluggable key_provider, encryptor, message_serializer, AES-GCM cipher
features.gap: KeyProvider is a concrete class with class-level state. Cipher is CBC+HMAC with a custom byte layout, so ciphertext is not interoperable with Rails data. No envelope-encryption provider (KMS) and no swappable encryptor. Deferred: Changing the cipher or payload layout breaks existing ciphertext. Needs a versioned payload design and a rotation plan first. Rails-compatible messages are a separate decision.

features.feature: Encryption: filter_parameters and inspect masking of encrypted attributes
features.gap: No filter_attributes; grep finds no inspect override on models. Plaintext appears in inspect, logs of bound values and exceptions.

features.feature: Instrumentation notifications (sql / transaction / instantiation / strict_loading_violation events with payload)
Verbose query logs (source location of SQL) and log tags with binds
features.gap: SQL log shows query with colorized params but no calling file:line, no query-name label (User Load), no cached-hit marker.

features.feature: Optimistic locking on destroy/touch, locking_enabled?, and stale-record refresh
features.gap: StaleObjectError is raised on update only (optimistic.cr); destroy and touch do not include lock_version in their WHERE, so a stale destroy succeeds. No locking_enabled?, no automatic lock_version increment on touch.

features.feature: Pessimistic lock! raises on unsaved changes
features.gap: lock! just calls reload_with_lock, silently discarding unsaved attribute changes; AR raises to prevent that data loss (unless lock! is given a lock clause on a clean record). Also no lock: option on association reload.
No lock preventing two processes from running migrations at once on PG or MySQL.
No Hash(String, String?) column type, no migration type or operators. Deferred: Low value, PG only, and JSONB covers the main use.

features.feature: Database-specific types: PostgreSQL ranges, network (inet/cidr/macaddr), interval, native enum, citext
features.gap: Only PG::Interval appears in the adapter's allowed type list and no spec covers it. No Range(T,T) column mapping, no Socket::IPAddress column, no PG CREATE TYPE enum mapping or citext. Deferred: Effort L, low value, and range bound normalization makes dirty tracking risky. Take individual types on demand.

features.feature: Test assertions for queries (assert_queries_count, assert_no_queries, assert_queries_match)

features.gap: Grant relies on external Micrate and the Amber CLI for these operations; no Grant-level programmatic create/drop/purge/prepare API and no structure-dump load.

features.feature: Integration cache keys and to_param (cache_key, cache_version, collection_cache_key)
Marshal/YAML coders and Ruby-only serialization internals (Marshal.dump of records, YAMLColumn, encode_with)
features.not_applicable_reason: Ruby Marshal/Psych object-graph serialization has no Crystal analog; JSON/YAML columns are covered by serialized_column.

features.gap: message: as a Proc or Symbol (I18n key) is still missing and is owned by V02.

Row text is covered (scope single/multi, case_sensitive, allow_nil, self-exclusion in uniqueness_spec.cr) but allow_blank: has no spec, and AR options conditions: (lambda scope on the uniqueness query), index_errors:, and validating against a scope named as an association are absent. The case_sensitive: false path builds raw `LOWER(col) = LOWER(?)` with an unquoted column name. Not run per-adapter (SQLite only here).

All failing constraints collapse into one combined message (e.g. 'must be greater than 0 and an integer') carrying a single error code; AR adds one error per failed constraint with its own type (:greater_than, :not_an_integer ...). Bounds must be compile-time literals: no Symbol (other attribute) or Proc operand for greater_than/less_than/equal_to/other_than (AR supports both). No spec for equal_to, other_than, less_than_or_equal_to, allow_blank, in:. only_numeric string-before-typecast semantics are replaced by ConversionError.

features.feature: Unified validates macro (AR style: validates :field, presence: true, length: {min:2})

features.gap: No Grant::Validator(T) generic, no AR options hash or reader, and errors are not tied to the validator's type code. The typed reader returns nil for non-column (virtual) attributes. With strict:, the errors the validator added remain in record.errors when it raises.

features.feature: Conditional validations (if:, unless: as Symbol method references)
Errors API (add, [], full_messages, where, of_type, include?, attribute_names, group_by_attribute, merge!, to_hash, to_json)
features.gap: Listed methods exist and 62 examples pass, but semantics diverge: of_type(attr, message : String) matches on MESSAGE while AR of_type(attr, type) matches the type symbol; where(attr) has no type/options filter; to_hash takes no full_messages arg; to_json emits [{field,message}] not AR's {attr => [messages]}; add() takes no options and cannot generate messages from a type symbol; merge! copies Error references (shared mutable objects).

Errors#details now exists and returns {"attr" => [{:error => type}]} with :invalid fallback (parity_spec.cr 'errors.details (typed codes)', 26 examples pass on SQLite). Remaining: no options in the detail hash (AR: {error: :too_short, count: 3}, {error: :greater_than, count: 0, value: -1}); details keys are Strings not Symbols; only some validators pass a type (numericality reports only the first constraint code); no `Error#details`/`Error#type` typed options; errors added by validates_with need explicit type: or fall back to :invalid.

features.feature: strict: option on validators (raises instead of adding to errors)
Full lifecycle callbacks (before/after save, create, update, destroy, after_initialize, after_find, before/after_validation, after_touch)
Callback halting via abort! (equivalent to AR throw :abort)
Conditional callbacks (if:, unless: on lifecycle callbacks)
after_rollback fires on explicit transaction rollback
Callback ordering (multiple callbacks on same event)

features.gap: Each event is publicly callable (`item.before_create`, spec 'manually triggered' passes as written) which runs the before/after chain for that one event. Still missing: `run_callbacks(:save) { ... }` wrapping a block between before and after chains (incl. around callbacks and halting return value), and a symbol-dispatched runtime form.

Implemented as a before_validation hook only, so values are normalized on valid?/save, not on assignment (AR normalizes in the attribute setter and on read of existing values). Only String-valued attributes; one attribute per call (no `normalizes :a, :b`); no with: lambda form (block only); no apply_to_nil:; no Model.normalize_value_for(:attr, value); where/find_by conditions are not normalized (AR normalizes query values); save(validate: false) skips normalization; if: option is not in AR.
validate! does not exist (owned by V01).

features.feature: on: array of contexts and on: for before_validation/after_validation callbacks
Multi-attribute form for every validates_*_of macro
Error message generation from type symbol, message: as Symbol/Proc, errors.add(attr, :type, **options)
features.gap: Messages are hard-coded English strings at macro expansion. errors.add(:name, :blank) does not compile (message is String); `message:` on validators must be a String literal, not a Symbol key or `->(object, data)` proc; no %{count} interpolation.

features.feature: Errors extras (delete, added?, of_type by type, messages_for, full_message, import/copy!, objects, uniq!, count by attribute)
features.gap: Absent from src/grant/errors.cr: delete(attr, type=nil), added?(attr, type, **opts), messages_for(attr), full_message(attr, msg), import(error, attribute:), copy!(other), objects, uniq!, generate_message, errors.messages Hash accessor, errors.to_hash(true).

features.feature: ActiveModel::Error object API (attribute, type, options, raw_type, message, detail, full_message, strict_match?)
features.gap: Grant::Error has field, message, type; missing options, attribute alias, raw_type, detail, full_message(instance), match?(attr, type, **opts). to_s capitalizes only the first letter of the raw column name (no humanize: 'first_name' becomes 'First_name').
No locale lookup, no Model.human_attribute_name, no per-model/per-attribute message overrides, no format template ('%{attribute} %{message}').

features.feature: validates_each block form (validates_each :a, :b do |record, attr, value|)
Validator reflection (validators, validators_on, validate callbacks introspection)
features.gap: __validators_for_validation is internal; no public list of validators per attribute, no kind/options metadata, so form builders and API docs cannot derive maxlength/required.
Not in CALLBACK_NAMES (src/grant/callbacks.cr) or the commit dispatch in src/grant/commit_callbacks.cr.

Callback macros take only if:/unless:; after_rollback fires regardless of the action while AR after_rollback supports on:. Also AR dedups commit callbacks when the same record is saved several times in one transaction; not verified in Grant.

features.feature: Callback conditions as arrays and combined if:+unless: lists

features.gap: CALLBACKS entries are always appended; no prepend: (used by dependent: :destroy ordering guidance in Rails).

features.feature: skip_callback / set_callback / define_callbacks / reset_callbacks (custom callback chains)
features.gap: No way to skip an inherited callback in a subclass or define new callback chains; runtime per-call skipping is impossible with compile-time chains. Callback chain is a compile-time constant, so run-time mutation is Ruby-metaprogramming-shaped. Deferred: Effort L, low value, and compile-time chains make Ruby-style runtime mutation a poor fit. Revisit after CB01.

features.feature: Callback objects (before_save MyCallback.new / class with before_save(record))
features.gap: Callbacks accept a method Symbol or a block only; no object with a before_save(record) protocol for shared, testable callback classes. Deferred: Low value. A method Symbol or block already covers the use; the callback-object protocol adds compile-time surface for little benefit.

features.feature: Model.normalize_value_for and normalization on query conditions
features.gap: No public normalize_value_for(attr, value); where(email: " A@X.COM ") and find_by do not normalize the search value while AR does.

Connection names are not checked against the registry when declared, which misses the perf guardrail. Only the literal shape is checked at compile time; registry verification is an explicit boot call, verify_connections! or verify_all!. Pools are still established separately. Sharding::Model does not read the connects_to(shards:) map. A shard named :default is not used when no shard is active.

database: still takes a String, not a role hash. Role routing is proven only against two SQLite files, so the pg run does not exercise a Postgres pair. Sharding::Model shard routing through connected_to(shard:) is now proven by adapter URL on SQLite files, but not through a full sharded query or on Postgres.

features.feature: Read replica load balancing (multiple replicas, strategies)

features.gap: QueryRouter.resolve_range_shards still accepts only String/Int64 bounds, so a Time-typed where range scatter-gathers instead of pruning. Only >=/<= pairs on the first key are pruned. Prefixed composite IDs (generate_composite_id("ORD")) do not route through time_range. Ranges are now half-open [from, to): a from == to range is rejected, and adjacent ranges share a boundary.

Probe on real SQLite shards: order(id).limit(3).offset(2) returned [4,6,7] (OFFSET applied per shard, not globally). sum/average/minimum/maximum raise 'No shard context'. shards_by __builder hard-codes DbType::Sqlite so PG/MySQL builds use the SQLite assembler. Specs use virtual adapters only, so merged real rows are unproven.

features.feature: Sharding integration specs (cross-strategy, error handling, transactions, concurrent)
features.gap: Suites use VirtualShardAdapter (records SQL, no rows) except one SQLite move_to_shard spec; no spec for real data merge, offset, aggregates, find_each, instance save routing, or restart-stable hashing; PostgreSQL untested.

features.not_applicable_reason: ActiveRecord 8 does not provide atomic distributed transactions across independent databases.

features.gap: Saving a changed shard key is not guarded. Additionally, save/update on a loaded sharded record raises 'No shard context' outside with_shard (current_shard is nil after loading), so the guard needs record shard tracking first.
No cross-shard join guard exists.
Grant has no Amber/HTTP::Handler that routes GET/HEAD to reading and other verbs to writing, nor per-session last-write tracking.

features.not_applicable_reason: ActiveRecord 8 does not provide automatic elastic resharding or consistent-hash migration.

features.gap: Rails migrates every database in the environment configuration, including shard entries, with a per-database migrations_paths and schema dump; Grant's Migrator is per-model adapter only and has no run-on-all-configured-connections task.

features.feature: Per-shard connection with read replica (shards: {shard_one: {writing:, reading:}})
features.gap: Shard-config maps and shard adapter lookup are covered; Sharding::Model routing ignores reading role and connected_to(role:) for sharded models (ShardManager.adapter passes current_role but no test proves a shard replica read). No PostgreSQL evidence.

Probe on real SQLite shards: find_each(batch_size: 3) yielded 12 rows for 10 records (duplicates and nondeterministic), because inside each with_shard the batch query is scatter-gathered across all shards again and offsets are per shard. Cited evidence covers non-sharded find_each only. No start/finish/order/error_on_ignore options on the sharded path; serial across shards.

Grant's main shard switches for Sharding::Model, Grant::ShardManager.with_shard and Sharding::Model.on_shard, are not guarded. A request pinned with prohibit_shard_swapping can still move to another shard through them.
No request middleware that picks a shard per request (e.g. from tenant/subdomain) and optionally locks it.

features.feature: Multi-database configuration (database.yml configurations, replica: true, DATABASE_URL)
features.gap: No declarative per-environment multi-database config. Connections are registered in code only via establish_connection(s); no configs_for(env, name), replica marker, DATABASE_URL merge, or database_tasks flag.

features.feature: Abstract base class connection inheritance (primary_abstract_class / abstract connects_to)
features.gap: primary_abstract_class only marks the class and changes no routing. A child's connects_to replaces only the settings it names, so the parent's shards still apply.

features.feature: Explicit connection API (establish_connection / remove_connection / connected? / connection_pool / retrieve_connection_pool)

features.gap: Block-scoped with_connection exists (adapter, model, Grant.connection, pool). No lease_connection / release_connection permanent lease API, by design (starves the pool).

features.feature: Connection pool introspection and lifecycle (stat, size, idle/busy, reaping, max_age, min_connections)
Connection error hierarchy (ConnectionNotEstablished, ConnectionTimeoutError, ConnectionNotDefined, ReadOnlyError)
Automatic shard routing for instance save/update/destroy on shards_by models
features.gap: Probe: new record save! outside with_shard raises 'No shard context'; a record loaded via a sharded query has current_shard nil and update raises the same outside with_shard. The before_save/after_save macros defined inside Sharding::Model are not callbacks and never run.
Probe: ProbeRec.sum(:tenant_id) raises 'No shard context'. Only count, exists?, pluck are routed.
Probe: order(id).limit(3).offset(2) returned [4,6,7] instead of [3,4,5]; offset is applied per shard and never globally. ORDER + LIMIT merge works in memory (first N after sort).

features.feature: update / update! (instance-level, sets attributes then saves)
import (bulk INSERT with batch_size, update_on_duplicate, ignore_on_duplicate)
insert_all / insert_all! (AR8 bulk insert without callbacks)
Dirty tracking (changed?, changes, attribute_was, per-attribute helpers)
features.gap: <attr>_came_from_user? is not implemented. changes, _change and _was return values as the DirtyValue union, not the column type. changed_attributes returns names, not ActiveRecord's hash. No spec covers _was on a non-nilable column with a converter round trip.

features.feature: Attribute API (virtual attributes, default values, converters)

features.gap: Implemented: predicates, bang setters, positive scopes, values list, mapping, default, integer or string storage, validates_enum. Differences from AR: bang setters (published!) only assign in memory while AR persists via update!; no negated scopes (Post.not_draft); no prefix:/suffix: options so two enums with a shared member name collide at compile time; no scopes: false; no validate: option on the macro; no _previously_was; Model.statuses returns an Array where AR returns the name-to-value mapping; where(status: :published) symbol or string lookup is not shown in the spec (needs the enum type).

Source: one attribute per call, block only, applied only to String values, run in before_validation (so save(validate: false), update_columns, import, create with skip paths bypass it). AR normalizes on assignment and on query arguments (User.find_by(email: " A@B ") matches the stored normalized value), supports multiple attributes, with: callable, apply_to_nil:, and exposes Model.normalize_value_for(:attr, value). The if: option is Grant-specific.

features.feature: Store accessors (store_accessor for JSON column sub-keys)
features.gap: No store or store_accessor macro. serialized_column exists and could back it.

features.feature: Token for (generates_token_for / find_by_token_for — AR8 data-invalidating tokens)

features.gap: Opt-in include (AR is automatic on every model); composite primary keys not supported.

belongs_to counter_cache: (create/destroy maintenance, including polymorphic adjust helper) exists. features.gap: advanced_multi_database_spec.cr runs entirely on SQLite in-memory. There is no spec that registers a SQLite connection and a PostgreSQL connection in one process and drives two models against them (independent transactions, no cross-adapter placeholder or type leakage). compile_target_adapters_spec.cr proves only compile-time adapter selection.
There is no per-role pool configuration, which belongs to the pool batch.

features.feature: Pessimistic locking (FOR UPDATE, FOR SHARE, SKIP LOCKED, NOWAIT)
features.gap: Specs cover SQL text per adapter and single-fiber with_lock on SQLite (where lock modes are a no-op); no spec proves blocking, NOWAIT/SKIP LOCKED behavior on a real PG/MySQL server. Defects by inspection: with_lock does result.not_nil!, so a block returning nil raises; lock!/with_lock silently overwrite unsaved changes (AR raises 'Locking a record with unsaved changes is not supported'); NOWAIT/SKIP LOCKED failures surface as raw DB::Error because LockNotAvailableError/LockWaitTimeoutError are never raised; lock accepts only the 6-value enum (no free-form lock string, no lock(false)); with_lock takes no transaction options.

Update path is guarded and specced (12 examples pass on SQLite). Not implemented: destroy of a stale record does not raise StaleObjectError (AR checks lock_version on destroy); no lock_optimistically toggle or locking_enabled?; touch/update_columns/update_all interplay unspecced. Opt-in via include Grant::Locking::Optimistic (a deliberate Crystal difference, fine) but it force-adds a lock_version column. Configurable column is tracked separately.

features.feature: Adapter feature matrix (PG vs MySQL vs SQLite differences)

features.gap: Nothing verifies a connection before use after it has sat idle (ActiveRecord verifies lazily). After a server restart or failover, each dead idle connection in the pool fails one write with Grant::ConnectionFailed instead of being detected and replaced. With max_idle_pool_size defaulting to pool_size, that can be up to pool_size failed writes. BEGIN on a stale connection in Transaction also fails. keepalive (an opt-in) only reduces this.

Connection-context and virtual-shard routing specs pass on mocks/SQLite; no PostgreSQL or MySQL multi-database shard integration, and no spec where two shards resolve to two real physical databases with per-shard reader routing.

features.feature: Postgres transaction atomicity and same-connection writes

features.gap: BEGIN is sent immediately on every transaction block, even ones that run no query or only reads that a cache satisfies; AR defers BEGIN until the first statement. Deferred: Low value, effort L, and lazy checkout mid-block risks starving the pool. Revisit after T01 lands and benchmarks show empty-transaction cost.

features.feature: Current transaction object and per-transaction callbacks (Rails 7.2)

features.feature: Relation#lock with a custom SQL clause or false
features.gap: Grant's lock takes only the 6-value LockMode enum. There is no free-form vendor lock string (e.g. 'FOR NO KEY UPDATE', MySQL 'LOCK IN SHARE MODE') and no lock(false) to clear a lock inherited from a scope.

Grant's main shard switches for Sharding::Model, Grant::ShardManager.with_shard and Sharding::Model.on_shard, are not guarded. A request pinned with prohibit_shard_swapping can still move to another shard through them.

features.gap: Same-column equality/IN replacement, the proc form, keyword form and select merge work. Scope lambdas are not applied to the JOIN ON clause. Polymorphic belongs_to joins and Arel/block joins are not implemented. There is no automatic table aliasing when one table is reached through two different associations or paths (e.g. joins(:comments, posts: :comments) emits the table twice with no alias and the database rejects it; AR aliases it as comments_posts). Only identical clauses are de-duplicated. Raw fragments have no binds.

Associations declared with a scope raise ArgumentError. ActiveRecord applies the association scope through joins/left_outer_joins. has_one and composite-key associations have no spec. A through association with a polymorphic or nested source raises. The old has/missing(table:, foreign_key:) forms remain.

features.gap: The :includes, :preload, :eager_load and :strict_loading components are not recognized, so only(:where) keeps includes and except(:includes) raises ArgumentError. AR supports both. Default-scope clauses are also left untouched. This needs the A01 (includes) batch.

Same as where.missing: scoped associations raise ArgumentError where ActiveRecord applies the scope. has_one and composite-key associations have no spec. Polymorphic belongs_to raises, which matches ActiveRecord.

features.gap: Only unscoped { } exists; no scoping { } that makes a relation the current scope for the block (responds_to? false).

features.not_applicable_reason: references exists so includes can guess JOIN vs preload by parsing string conditions at runtime; Grant selects the strategy explicitly (includes/preload/eager_load).

features.gap: Absent (responds_to? false); no WITH clause support in the assemblers.

WhereChain offers string-field predicates (where.gt(:age, 18)) but no typed column objects that compose (Post.arel_table[:id].gt(1).and(...)), no OR-ing of predicates, no reuse across where/order/select/having/joins conditions. Deferred: Effort L. Its value depends on stable relation immutability (Q01) and where composition (Q02). Consider a typed-column design in a later release, not this program.
Deferred: Low value and effort M. Merge with Cross-database associations (has_many / has_one through with disable_joins: true), which is a duplicate. Revisit after A02.

Single hop only, and the source must be a belongs_to. Nested (multi-hop) through, source_type:, a has_many source (raises ThroughWriteError), disable_joins, and cross-database loading are still missing. Appending a target that is already linked, while the collection is not loaded, inserts a duplicate join row (ActiveRecord behaves the same, with no unique index).

Everything in the implementer's list. In addition, the check for whether through: names an association runs at macro time against methods already defined on this class only. If the through association is declared later, or on a parent class, the code silently falls back to the legacy table-name reader: an N+1 on preload, and bad SQL if no table has that name.
The create_join_table migration helper is missing (the spec creates the join table by hand). Join columns are Int64 only. There is no scope argument and no extend option.

Done and spec'd: UUID/String keys via typed foreign_key declaration, preload of has_many/has_one as:, has_one as: setter and caching, polymorphic_name (STI root), registration, has_many as: returns AssociationCollection with the type predicate in SQL, dependent delete_all/delete/nullify/destroy. Not covered: dependent :restrict and :restrict_with_exception on the as: side are implemented but have no spec; an STI subclass (not the root) that declares has_many as: registers under its own name so a stored root name will not resolve through load_polymorphic; a String foreign key over UUID has_many owners is not supported (only belongs_to normalizes keys to text).

The spellings already match AR (has_many :delete_all, has_one :delete), and dependent_delete_all_spec.cr covers both (ran: pass). Remaining: dependent: :destroy_async (and ensuring_owner_was) is absent; any unrecognized dependent: value (e.g. has_many :delete, :restrict_with_error) falls through the macro elsif chain and is silently ignored (probe P3); dependent is not applied on has_many :through join rows.

Code has closed part of the tracked gap: :restrict_with_exception is implemented (raises Grant::Associations::RestrictError) and tested in association_parity_spec.cr. Still absent: the AR name :restrict_with_error is not recognized and is silently ignored (probe P3: destroy returned true and deleted the owner); Grant's :restrict is a non-AR alias. The exception class is RestrictError, not a DeleteRestrictionError-named equivalent; the error message is added to :base only.

New and dirty (autosave: true) children are saved via after_save with save!, so an invalid child raises after the owner row is written (inside the around_save transaction) instead of owner.save returning false with an error on the owner (AR validate: true default). No autosave: false semantics, no mark_for_destruction/marked_for_destruction?, no per-child has_many replace/removal on save, and the belongs_to autosave only saves unpersisted parents.

Create/destroy/FK-change adjustments work (regressions A-10, A-17, options spec) and a polymorphic counter cache exists (integration_spec), but: reset_counters and increment_counter/decrement_counter class helpers are absent (update_counters exists); counter_cache: true derives the column with a naive `underscore + "s_count"` (Category -> categorys_count, AR gives categories_count); conditional counter_cache: {active: false} unsupported; has_many counter_cache: option (so size reads the cached column) unsupported; collection delete/delete_all/clear do not decrement; in-memory parent counters are not updated; polymorphic counter cache requires Int64 ids.

setup_touch runs after_save/after_destroy on the current parent only (self.association). When the FK changes, AR also touches the previous parent; Grant does not. No spec covers touch on destroy or the old-parent case. Touch runs one UPDATE per save even when nothing changed.

The switch from includes to a JOIN only happens on the load path (select/first/each). count, exists? and pluck on an includes relation whose where names the association table still do not join; a probe confirmed count raises ArgumentError 'Unknown query field "ni_cities.name"', where AR counts over the join. When the where contains an OR, the association now loads all its rows (a superset) because a flat WHERE cannot be replayed; AR would hold only the joined rows. An association scope that uses .or still renders flat on the preload query (a OR b AND fk IN (...)), which over-fetches rows; that is a builder precedence issue owned by Q01. eager_load of a polymorphic belongs_to raises stdlib ArgumentError, not a Grant::ErrorBase error.

Done: association strict_loading: true/false option, Model.strict_loading_by_default, strict_loading!(value, mode), :n_plus_one_only, propagation to loaded records (lazy and preloaded), Grant.settings.strict_loading_violation = :raise | :log, polymorphic has_many/has_one/belongs_to readers assert; spec has no responds_to? guards. Gap: strict_loading_by_default is keyed by class name and not inherited by subclasses (set it on each model, or on Grant::Base for a global default); Relation#strict_loading has no mode argument (builder.cr strict_loading region belongs to Q01).

Only has_many and has_one are handled (source branches on :has_many/:has_one); belongs_to nested attributes are unsupported. reject_if accepts only :all_blank; a proc is silently treated as nil. No index_errors, no RecordNotFound when an id is not part of the association, and it needs an explicit `enable_nested_saves` call plus a typed declaration (acceptable Crystal idiom). Spec covers create/update/destroy/limit/update_only/all_blank/validation propagation for has_many and has_one only.
No delegated_type macro. Everything it needs (polymorphic belongs_to, has_one as:, enum-style predicates) exists separately, but only for Int64 keys.

Scope now applies in SQL on preload, lazy readers, and for belongs_to and has_one (zero-arg expression form and ->(q : Builder(T)) form). Still missing: extend: module/block extensions, instance-dependent scopes ->(q, owner), scope on polymorphic as: associations, scope honored by dependent:.

_ids and _ids= are not generated for has_many as:. The reader returns Array(Columns::Type). Numeric String ids are not cast to the key type. The writer uses update_all, so it skips target validations, callbacks and the updated_at touch (ActiveRecord's replace saves each record).
Built records do not show up in reads of a collection that has not been loaded. Array create saves each record inside one transaction rather than doing a multi-row insert.

features.gap: Not generated (probe P6: responds_to?(:build_prb_detail) and :create_prb_detail are false).

Explicit raw scope and tenancy boundaries for model and connection SQL
